key_facts: A patient on (or recently off) **pembrolizumab, nivolumab, ipilimumab** or **dabrafenib + trametinib** with **any new symptom**.
Checkpoint inhibitors **release T-cell brakes**, so autoimmune inflammation can hit any organ, even months after stopping.
Ask **‘are you on cancer treatment?’**; contact the **24-hour acute oncology hotline** rather than treating alone; check interactions.
**Colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, myocarditis, hypophysitis / adrenal crisis, new type 1 diabetes / DKA, SJS / TEN.**

ul: **Checkpoint inhibitors** (anti-PD-1: pembrolizumab, nivolumab; anti-CTLA-4: ipilimumab; anti-LAG-3: relatlimab) release T-cell "brakes".
**BRAF/MEK inhibitors** block MAPK signalling in BRAF-mutant tumours.

fig.caption: Checkpoint inhibitor antibodies block the brake on T cells so they can attack melanoma; the same release can inflame normal organs.

sections.title: Clinical features

blocks.h: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs): mechanism and timing

blocks: These come from autoimmune inflammation of any organ. They can start **weeks to months after the first dose, and even after stopping**. Combination ipi+nivo causes grade 3–4 irAEs in more than half of patients.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations
blocks: Use a low threshold. Patients carry an **immunotherapy alert card** and a **24-hour acute oncology hotline** (UKONS triage tool). Always ask "are you on cancer treatment?"

ul: **“Are you on cancer treatment?”**; alert card + **24-hour hotline** (UKONS triage).
TFTs, glucose, cortisol, sodium, LFT, U&E as directed.
Infection (e.g. *C. difficile*), other drug reactions, progression.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses

ddx.name: Infection
ddx.f: *C. difficile*, chest infection: but don’t assume.

blocks: Infection (e.g. *C. difficile* in a patient with diarrhoea), drug reactions, and disease progression.

ul: **Never start immunosuppression independently. Contact the acute oncology team**, who will grade the event and prescribe high-dose corticosteroids/other immunosuppressants (per ESMO/UKONS).

**Steroid stewardship:** patients on high-dose steroids for irAEs need **PPI/gastroprotection, glucose monitoring, bone protection if prolonged, PJP prophylaxis (co-trimoxazole) if ≥20 mg prednisolone for ≥4 weeks**, a **steroid emergency card**, and "sick-day" rules for adrenal insufficiency.
**Vaccines:** inactivated vaccines (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal) are fine. Live vaccines need specialist advice.

**BRAF/MEK inhibitors:** **Pyrexia** (dabrafenib + trametinib) needs interrupting treatment per the protocol and contacting the oncology team; **Photosensitivity** (vemurafenib): sun protection; New SCC/KA and new naevi (BRAF monotherapy); **QT prolongation** (vemurafenib, encorafenib): check interacting drugs; **CYP3A4 interactions**: dabrafenib is an inducer, which lowers levels of hormonal contraceptives (use a non-hormonal method; contraception is needed during treatment), warfarin and others. Use the BNF/SmPC interaction checker; **LVEF reduction and ocular toxicity** (MEK inhibitors: serous retinopathy); **Hand–foot skin reaction.**
**Pregnancy:** effective contraception during treatment and for months afterwards (per SmPC; e.g. 4 months after pembrolizumab).

ladder.t: **Never start immunosuppression independently**: acute oncology grades and prescribes (ESMO / UKONS). Skin grade 1–2: emollient + topical steroid; urgent if blistering / mucosal.
High-dose steroids: **PPI**, **glucose monitoring**, bone protection if prolonged, **PJP prophylaxis (co-trimoxazole)** if ≥ 20 mg prednisolone ≥ 4 weeks, **steroid emergency card**, sick-day rules.

**Fever** on dabrafenib + trametinib: interrupt per protocol and call oncology. **Dabrafenib induces CYP3A4**: hormonal contraception unreliable (non-hormonal method); warfarin and others: interaction checker.
Inactivated vaccines fine; live vaccines: specialist advice. Effective contraception during and for months after (e.g. 4 months after pembrolizumab).

refer.t: Chest pain / suspected myocarditis, DKA, adrenal crisis, SJS / TEN.
**Diarrhoea, breathlessness, severe headache, chest pain, new thirst / polyuria** on immunotherapy: acute oncology.
Fever on dabrafenib + trametinib: protocol + oncology team.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Diarrhoea, breathlessness, severe headache, chest pain or new thirst/polyuria in a patient on immunotherapy: **same-day acute oncology** contact.
Fever on dabrafenib + trametinib: follow the protocol (interrupt) and contact the oncology team.

pearls: Explain that side-effects can be serious but are usually treatable *if caught early*: "ring the hotline, not the GP's routine line".
Vitiligo during anti-PD-1 therapy is common and often correlates with better response. Protect the depigmented skin from sun.

quiz.a: Same-day acute oncology contact; don’t just give loperamide.
CYP3A4 induction lowers hormonal levels: non-hormonal method.
Interrupt per protocol and contact oncology.
